question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**higher**" means greater in amount, frequency, or degree. (उच्चतर)
 
• In the context of the passage, politicians claiming "even higher" literacy rates fits the idea of boasting about increased percentages.
 
• The other options: "**lower**" (lesser in amount), "**moderate**" (average), and "**better**" (improved but not necessarily in percentage terms) do not convey the sense of a numerical increase in literacy rates.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Politicians proclaim that their states have achieved 80 or 90 per cent literacy or even higher__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Lower (कम)**: means a reduced amount or level. This does not fit with the idea of politicians boasting about literacy rates.
 
• **Moderate (मध्यम)**: means average or not excessive. It does not fit with the context of claiming a significant literacy achievement.
 
• **Better (बेहतर)**: means improved. While positive, it does not necessarily imply a numerical increase that fits the context of literacy rates.
